params.script_inline:
import sys, json
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
hop = ((doc["envelope"].get("header") or {}).get("hop") or {})
name = str(hop.get("tool_name") or "")
asked = name if name else "(none)"
text = "no tool named %s is wired into this hive" % asked
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": {"route": "tool_result", "operation": "unknown",
               "error_code": "unknown_tool", "tool_name": name,
               "tool_call_id": str(hop.get("tool_call_id") or "")},
    "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                  "id": str(hop.get("tool_call_id") or ""), "text": text}]}))

description.purpose: The target of this hive's guarded default edge: a call for a tool nobody wired comes back as ONE typed tool_result naming the tool that was asked for, on the same lane every other occupant answers on.
description.use_when: Never wired by hand and never addressed by name. It is reached only when no positive tool edge fired -- an unknown `hop.tool_name`, or a `tool_call` carrying none at all -- and only because the default edge's own guard held.
description.not_in_scope: Not a tool: no arguments are read, nothing is executed, nothing is fetched. No suggestion of a near-miss name either -- guessing what the model MEANT is the judgement this hive does not make. And it is not a drain: a cell that accepted the call and emitted nothing would be exactly the swallowing sink GH #284 removed from this repository.
description.emits_meaning: route tool_result: the one outward lane of the hive, so the caller's single return edge takes this the way it takes every answer. hop.error_code is always `unknown_tool` and hop.tool_name is the name that was asked for -- verbatim, including the empty string when the call carried none. hop.operation says `unknown`, which is what this hive's return edge conditions on, the same way it conditions on `bash` / `web_fetch` / `web_search` for the three tools.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: the tool_call turn as it arrived. It is not parsed -- what the call wanted is irrelevant once there is nothing to serve it.
examples: hop.tool_name == 'nonesuch' -> tool_result 'no tool named nonesuch is wired into this hive', hop { error_code: 'unknown_tool', tool_name: 'nonesuch' }
a tool_call with no hop.tool_name at all -> the same refusal, tool_name empty -- the caller learns its dispatcher lost the name, instead of watching the round stall
